entries.subject:
Primary request: show selective livestock breeding through one robust cream-white longwool breeding sheep and its small lamb, inspired by eighteenth-century improved Leicester sheep.
Subject: one adult hornless ewe in a calm side-on three-quarter stance facing left, a broad healthy body and long gently wavy wool locks. The face and legs are pale ivory, black eyes and a dark natural nose, no horns. Four anatomically correct adult legs, proportionate head and visible ears, simple readable hoof shapes. One smaller lamb stands slightly forward beside the adult, with a shorter soft cream fleece and the same natural pale face, all four of its legs coherent. The adult is the dominant subject; the lamb is the sole accessory and its head must not hide the adult legs. Keep both animals fully within the canvas and distinctly separate enough for the silhouette to read. Warm neutral wool shadows, subtly painted wool, no yellow staining.
Avoid: fantasy curled ram horns, goat, black-faced sheep, extra heads or legs, ear tags, collars, ribbons, medals, fences, grass, farm scene, feeding equipment, ground or cast shadows. Natural animal illustration in a strategy-game technology icon; no cute cartoon expression or realistic photographic rendering.

entries.subject:
Primary request: show early agricultural field drainage using hand-made terracotta horseshoe drains, not a modern sewer pipe or drainage landscape.
Subject: a short run of TWO clay roof-shaped drain tiles placed neatly end-to-end along a single diagonal from lower left toward upper right, each resting on its matching thin separate flat terracotta sole tile. The roof-shaped section has a rounded arch top and straight short side legs forming an inverted-U / horseshoe opening. The near open end is fully visible as a hollow arch, its dark interior is physically correct, not a black background drawn behind it. Flat ceramic sole closes the bottom of the passage. Readable joint between the two tiles, no sockets, flanges or perforations. Matte weathered warm reddish-brown unglazed clay with softly brushed grain and modest handmade irregularity.
One plain ditching spade is the sole accessory: a restrained brown wooden handle and neutral grey flat steel blade lies diagonally behind the short tile run without covering the front drain opening. Keep it compact, no huge thin pole. Both subject and accessory entirely isolated on transparency.
Avoid: PVC, plastic, shiny red glaze, round Victorian sewer sockets, modern drainage holes, huge stacks of pipes, mini cutaway landscape, grass, water streams, trenches, foundations, roof scene, labels or arrows. Do not turn the tile into an architectural tunnel or a brick bridge.
entries.prompt:

Asset type: existing Victoria 3 TECHNOLOGY icon, not a flat production-method pictogram.
Input images: Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET. Preserve the existing painted object design, viewpoint, materials, proportions and restrained brushed texture.
Scene/backdrop: genuine transparent alpha throughout the exterior and openings. Preserve transparency. No black painted background, checkerboard, ground plane, scene, frame, medallion or UI ring.
Lighting/palette: preserve natural terracotta, brown wood, neutral iron and dull brass; keep the original light direction. Pale blue-grey with ivory highlights is allowed ONLY for the added water. Do not put a blue cast on the objects.
Composition: the entire object AND all added water must fit inside a square canvas at least 1024 pixels, with clear transparent margins. Compact technology-icon silhouette readable at 48 and 64 pixels.
Constraints: add only the specified water and any minimal indicated outlet adjustment, not extra props. No text, labels, arrows, symbols, people, glow, large puddle, reservoir, crops or landscape. No restyling, no shiny 3D.
Primary request: make drainage visibly carry water. Add a clear small flow of water INSIDE the bottom of the near arch-shaped drain opening. It runs along the flat ceramic sole from the interior and then pours over the near FRONT EDGE as a short cohesive downward-curving ribbon, with two or three simple drops below its end. Water must visibly originate inside the drain passage, not from the top of the clay arch. Let pale silvery-blue highlights and a few broad ripples make it read as flowing water at icon size. Keep the arched roof and separate sole legible; the water does not fill the whole opening or hide the rim. Keep the flow restrained but not just a tiny almost invisible spot. Preserve both original clay sections, their joint, separate soles and the entire original spade. Do not add more drains or modify their geometry. No splash explosion or floor puddle.

entries.subject:
Primary request: depict an early automatic water-lifting hydraulic ram pump inspired by the Montgolfier-pattern arrangement shown in a circa-1822 museum drawing; compact mechanical irrigation apparatus, not a boiler or an electric centrifugal pump.
Subject: one coherent compact cast-iron hydraulic ram assembly in a modest front three-quarter view. A short thick horizontal inlet body with a bolted flange at the left sits on two small integral iron support feet. Above its central portion, a short neck carries ONE roughly spherical enclosed air chamber, unpainted neutral dark grey metal with restrained patina. A small vertical exposed waste-valve stem and its stop bracket stands on the right end of the same horizontal inlet body, clearly connected. A much thinner brass delivery outlet comes out from a valve housing below the spherical air chamber and bends upward toward the right; it does not merge into the waste-valve stem. All pieces join logically with readable separate inlet, waste valve, air chamber and delivery pipe. Keep the main air chamber and horizontal pipe bulky and legible, do not render dozens of tiny parts. Limited dull brass at valve and outlet, natural warm-neutral dark grey cast iron elsewhere. No paint or blue tint.
One compact functional apparatus only, no additional accessory. Transparent space between support feet and between pipes. Entire silhouette comfortably within the canvas.
Avoid: steam boiler, chimney, smokestack, flame, flywheel, hand crank, steam-cylinder rod, electric motor, pressure dial, huge pipe network, tank farm, modern sprinklers, landscape, water splash, gear ornaments, pedestal, lettering or diagram labels. Do not reproduce the reference drawing's blue section color. Do not copy museum labels. This simplified icon represents mechanical water lifting, not an exact engineering model.

Primary request: correct the physically incoherent water placement. REMOVE the existing water arch and drops completely. The water must not sit on the upper edge of an upward-facing opening.
Outlet correction: keep the existing tall thin brass delivery pipe connected to its existing housing. Change ONLY its uppermost terminal into a small smoothly curved gooseneck, turning over to the right and then DOWN. The pipe must be hollow, with a clearly readable open downward-facing end. Use the same dull brass, thickness and painted texture as the existing pipe; no large extra pipe network.
Water correction: show ONE short continuous coherent stream emerging DIRECTLY FROM INSIDE THAT DOWNWARD-FACING OPEN MOUTH, immediately falling downward under gravity into the empty space to the right of the pump. The metal lip remains visible on both sides of the stream. Water begins exactly at the mouth, with no transparent gap and no water pasted across the brass surface. A narrow silvery light blue-grey ribbon with broad off-white highlights and two or three modest drops below it. The stream should be clearly readable at 48 and 64 pixels without overwhelming the machine. Do not make a fountain arch, an upward jet, a huge splash, a detached droplet emblem or a floor puddle.
Invariants: preserve the cast-iron horizontal inlet body, left bolted flange, two support feet, roughly spherical enclosed air chamber, all joints and bolts, lower brass delivery housing, short waste-valve stem and bracket. Keep their design, size, viewpoint, proportions, brushed matte material, neutral warm iron and original lighting unchanged. Do not add water to the inlet, chamber or waste valve. No new props or ground.
Background: genuine transparent alpha throughout the exterior and openings. Preserve transparency; no painted black or white background or checkerboard. Square canvas at least 1024 pixels with generous margins. Entire assembly, gooseneck and all water fully inside the frame.
Style and color: the same restrained hand-painted Victoria 3 technology aesthetic. No global blue or teal cast, no glossy 3D, no restyling. Pale blue-grey is limited to the water. No scene, crops, reservoir, frame, medallion, symbols, arrows, text, logo or watermark.
